nt: The next few verses are the climax of this part of Exodus. A number of literary features mark it out. First, it is specially introduced with **and so it happened**, which is used to mark major breaks in the narrative. Second, it uses repetition: **firstborn** is repeated four times in [verse 29](../12/29.md) so that the reader cannot possibly miss what is happening. **Night** is repeated in [verse 29](../12/29.md), [30](../12/30.md), and [31](../12/31.md). **Got up/get up** is repeated in [verse 30](../12/30.md) and [31](../12/31.md). In [verses 31](../12/31.md) and [32](../12/32.md) “also” occurs five times (it is translated as “both” once in the ULT). Third, the places of both **Pharaoh** and **the captive** are elaborated on to slow the pace and create a vivid mental image for the reader. In [verse 30](../12/30.md) there is the listing of sorts of people who got up; note the use of the double negative for emphasis. Your translation should attempt to use the same or similar literary features of your own language that slow down the pace, create vivid imagery, and emphasize that this is a climax point.
